texts: bad: the restriction in "the keepers of the Middle Row" is dropped — the parse ties the lanterns to the Middle Row but leaves the keepers unattached, so which keepers did the lighting is not recorded, and the per-keeper rule it builds has each keeper lighting the whole lantern set. Rewrite as: "On day 460 of Year 2, the Middle Row keepers lit the lanterns of the Middle Row at sundown." — a name placed in front of the noun reliably gets the possessor link. (Separately, "day 460 of Year 2" is stored with the same day term used for a day-of-month, so a day numbered within the year is not distinguishable; no rewrite closes that.)
good. the burning is covered with the lantern group as the burner, and the mire-essence gets its own witness, which is what lets "the mire-essence" in the next sentence attach to it.

bad: "held" is read as a possession verb, so the parse says the mire-essence *owns* the salt-bloom rather than containing it — the wrong relation, and it feeds the possession machinery downstream. Rewrite as: "The mire-essence in the lanterns contained salt-bloom."
good. the slow burning is recorded as its own event on the mire-essence, with the manner adverb kept as stated.
good. the wind, its coldness, the row it struck and the night-time all land.

bad: only the group-level "stayed lit" state is emitted — there is no per-lantern form, so "was this lantern lit?" cannot be answered of any individual lantern, which matters because the next sentences work lantern by lantern. Rewrite as: "Each of the lanterns stayed lit." — the explicit "each of the" forces the state down onto every member of the lantern group.
good. the producing is covered and "mist-light" is decomposed so it counts as light.
good. "a handful" is recorded as a vague count on the nightmoth group, and the attracting takes the right roles.

mixed: the depositing, its place on the lanterns and the thread group are all covered, but the threads are filed as an object the leaving *changed* rather than one merely put down, and the per-moth rule has each moth leaving the whole thread set. If you want the deposit reading forced, write: "The nightmoths deposited silken threads on the lanterns."

mixed: the collecting itself parses cleanly — source, dawn, day 461 of Year 2 all carried — but the bare plural "Keepers" mints a second keeper group with no link to the Middle Row keepers of the opening sentence. If these are the same people, write: "The keepers of the Middle Row collected the silken threads from the lanterns at dawn on day 461 of Year 2."

good. Hesper, the threads, the sea-water, the first cauldron and the date are all carried. The rank on "the first cauldron" and the "in sea-water" medium land on forms the instruction set does not fully settle, but nothing you wrote is lost or distorted, so no rewrite is needed.
good. a fresh mire-essence witness is created in the cauldron, and "by evening" is correctly recorded as a deadline rather than a time point.
good. the storing corefers to the mire-essence that formed in the cauldron, and the clay vessel is typed and counted as a vessel.

good. the keepers resolve back to the Middle Row keepers of the opening sentence and the essence to the batch Hesper stored, with sundown on day 461 of Year 2 carried; "stored" itself gets no separate atom, but the coreference to Hesper's batch already carries it.
